flags.assumption: The Java helper input() calls System.console().readLine(), assuming the program is run from an interactive terminal. When standard input or output is redirected or piped, System.console() returns null and throws a NullPointerException, whereas Python's input() reads a line from stdin in both cases.
flags.suggestion: Replace System.console().readLine() with a static Scanner or BufferedReader on System.in, e.g. declare `private static final java.util.Scanner SC = new java.util.Scanner(System.in);` and return `SC.nextLine()` in `input()`.

System.console() is null when stdin/stdout is redirected (e.g., file redirection, pipes, IDEs, or automated judges), causing a NullPointerException. Using a shared Scanner(System.in).nextLine() or BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)).readLine() reads whole lines from System.in properly.
